airport.name: Cadete FAP Guillermo Del Castillo Paredes Airport

summary: Cadete FAP Guillermo Del Castillo Paredes Airport serves the city of Tarapoto in Peru's San Martín region, acting as the primary gateway to the Amazonian 'selva alta' area. Named in honor of a Peruvian Air Force cadet, the airport handles domestic flights connecting the region with Lima and other major Peruvian cities. Its strategic location makes it a popular jumping-off point for travelers exploring rainforest destinations, river excursions, and the Cordillera Escalera mountains.
faqs:
Q: What airlines operate at Cadete FAP Guillermo Del Castillo Paredes Airport?
A: Peruvian carriers including LATAM Perú and SKY Airline operate domestic flights from this airport, with the most common route being to Jorge Chávez International Airport in Lima.

Q: How far is the airport from Tarapoto city center?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometers from downtown Tarapoto, typically a short 15–20 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Is the airport open for international flights?
A: No, Cadete FAP Guillermo Del Castillo Paredes Airport handles domestic flights only.

Q: When is the best time to visit Tarapoto?
A: The dry season from May to October generally offers the best weather for exploring the surrounding Amazon region and waterfalls.
transport_tips: Taxis and mototaxis are readily available outside the terminal for the short trip into Tarapoto's city center. Fares are typically negotiated before boarding rather than metered, so confirm the price beforehand. Many hotels in the area also offer airport pickup services, which can be arranged in advance for added convenience.
local_tip: Pack a light rain jacket even in the dry season—Tarapoto's tropical climate can produce sudden showers, and humidity tends to spike unexpectedly throughout the year.
